title_en: Environmental Protection Tax Law of the People's Republic of China

articles.content_en: Article 1 This Law is enacted for the purpose of protecting and improving the environment, reducing pollutant emissions, and promoting the construction of ecological civilization.

Article 2 Enterprises, public institutions, and other business operators that directly discharge taxable pollutants to the environment within the territory of the People's Republic of China and other sea areas under the jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China shall be taxpayers of environmental protection tax and shall pay environmental protection tax in accordance with the provisions of this Law.

Article 3 "Taxable pollutants" as mentioned in this Law refer to air pollutants, water pollutants, solid wastes, and noise as specified in the "Table of Tax Items and Tax Amounts for Environmental Protection Tax" and the "Table of Taxable Pollutants and Equivalent Values" attached to this Law.

Article 5 Where urban or rural sewage centralized treatment facilities or domestic waste centralized treatment facilities established according to law discharge taxable pollutants into the environment in excess of the discharge standards prescribed by the State or local authorities, they shall pay environmental protection tax.
Where enterprises, public institutions, or other business operators store or dispose of solid wastes in a manner that does not meet the environmental protection standards prescribed by the State or local authorities, they shall pay environmental protection tax.

Article 6 The tax items and tax amounts of the environmental protection tax shall be implemented in accordance with the "Table of Tax Items and Tax Amounts for Environmental Protection Tax" attached to this Law.
The determination and adjustment of the specific applicable tax amounts for taxable air pollutants and water pollutants shall be proposed by the people's governments of provinces, autonomous regions, or municipalities directly under the Central Government, taking into comprehensive consideration the environmental carrying capacity, the current situation of pollutant discharge, and the requirements for economic, social, and ecological development objectives of the region, within the tax amount ranges specified in the "Table of Tax Items and Tax Amounts for Environmental Protection Tax" attached to this Law, submitted to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level for decision, and reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council for record.

Article 8 The number of pollution equivalents for taxable air pollutants and water pollutants shall be calculated by dividing the discharge amount of the pollutant by the pollution equivalent value of the pollutant. The specific pollution equivalent values for each type of taxable air pollutant and water pollutant shall be implemented in accordance with the "Table of Taxable Pollutants and Equivalent Values" attached to this Law.

Article 9 For each discharge outlet or taxable air pollutant without a discharge outlet, the pollutants shall be sorted in descending order of pollution equivalent numbers, and environmental protection tax shall be levied on the top three pollutants.
For taxable water pollutants at each discharge outlet, in accordance with the "Table of Taxable Pollutants and Equivalent Values" attached to this Law, they shall be distinguished as Category I water pollutants and other water pollutants, and sorted in descending order of pollution equivalent numbers. Environmental protection tax shall be levied on the top five Category I water pollutants and on the top three other water pollutants.
The people's government of a province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government may, based on the special needs for pollutant emission reduction in the region, increase the number of taxable pollutant items for which environmental protection tax is levied at the same discharge outlet, which shall be submitted to the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level for decision and reported to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress and the State Council for record.

Article 13 Where the concentration value of taxable air pollutants or water pollutants discharged by a taxpayer is less than 30% of the pollutant discharge standards prescribed by the State or local authorities, the environmental protection tax shall be reduced by 75%. Where the concentration value of taxable air pollutants or water pollutants discharged by a taxpayer is less than 50% of the pollutant discharge standards prescribed by the State or local authorities, the environmental protection tax shall be reduced by 50%.

Article 14 The environmental protection tax shall be collected and managed by the tax authorities in accordance with the "Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection" and the relevant provisions of this Law.
The competent department of ecological environment shall be responsible for the monitoring and management of pollutants in accordance with this Law and relevant laws and regulations on environmental protection.
The local people's governments at or above the county level shall establish a working mechanism for the division of labor and cooperation among the tax authorities, the competent department of ecological environment, and other relevant units to strengthen the collection and management of environmental protection tax and ensure that the tax is paid into the state treasury in a timely and full amount.

Article 15 The competent department of ecological environment and the tax authorities shall establish a tax-related information sharing platform and a work coordination mechanism.
The competent department of ecological environment shall regularly deliver to the tax authorities environmental protection-related information such as pollutant discharge permits, pollutant discharge data, environmental violations, and administrative penalties of pollutant-discharging units.
The tax authorities shall regularly deliver to the competent department of ecological environment environmental protection tax-related information such as taxpayers' tax returns, tax payment into the treasury, tax reduction and exemption amounts, tax arrears, and risk points.
Article 16 The time when the tax liability arises shall be the date when a taxpayer discharges taxable pollutants.
Article 17 A taxpayer shall declare and pay environmental protection tax to the tax authorities in the place where the taxable pollutants are discharged.

Article 18 Environmental protection tax shall be calculated on a monthly basis and declared and paid on a quarterly basis. If it cannot be calculated and paid on a fixed period, it may be declared and paid on each occurrence.
When declaring and paying tax, a taxpayer shall submit to the tax authorities the types and quantities of taxable pollutants discharged, the concentration values of air pollutants and water pollutants, and other tax-related materials requested by the tax authorities based on actual needs.

Article 19 If a taxpayer declares and pays tax quarterly, it shall handle tax declaration and pay tax to the tax authorities within 15 days from the end of each quarter. If a taxpayer declares and pays tax on each occurrence, it shall handle tax declaration and pay tax to the tax authorities within 15 days from the date when the tax liability arises.
A taxpayer shall truthfully make tax declarations according to law and bear the responsibility for the authenticity and completeness of the declarations.

Article 20 The tax authorities shall compare the tax declaration data and materials of taxpayers with the relevant data and materials delivered by the competent department of ecological environment.
If the tax authorities find that the tax declaration data and materials of a taxpayer are abnormal or that the taxpayer fails to handle tax declaration within the prescribed time limit, they may request the competent department of ecological environment to conduct a review, and the competent department of ecological environment shall issue a review opinion to the tax authorities within 15 days from the date of receiving the data and materials from the tax authorities. The tax authorities shall adjust the taxpayer's payable tax amount in accordance with the data and materials reviewed by the competent department of ecological environment.

Article 21 Where the amount of pollutants discharged is verified and calculated in accordance with the provisions of Item (4) of Article 10 of this Law, the tax authority shall, jointly with the competent department of ecological environment, verify the types, quantities and taxable amount of pollutants discharged.

Article 22 The specific measures for taxpayers engaged in offshore engineering to discharge taxable air pollutants, water pollutants or solid wastes into the sea areas under the jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China, and to declare and pay environmental protection tax, shall be prescribed by the tax authority of the State Council jointly with the competent department of ecological environment of the State Council.

Article 23 Where a taxpayer, a tax authority, a competent department of ecological environment and their staff members violate the provisions of this Law, legal liability shall be pursued in accordance with the provisions of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection, the Law of the People's Republic of China on Environmental Protection and relevant laws and regulations.

Article 24 People's governments at all levels shall encourage taxpayers to increase investment in environmental protection construction, and shall provide financial and policy support for taxpayers' investment in automatic pollutant monitoring equipment.

Article 25 For the purposes of this Law, the following terms mean:
(1) Pollution equivalent means a comprehensive indicator or measurement unit used to measure the environmental pollution of different pollutants based on the degree of harm to the environment caused by pollutants or pollution discharge activities and the technical and economic feasibility of treatment. Different pollutants with the same pollution equivalent in the same medium have substantially equivalent pollution levels.
(2) Discharge coefficient means the statistical average of the amount of pollutants that should be discharged per unit of product under normal technical, economic and management conditions.
(3) Material balance means a method of estimating the raw materials used, products produced and waste generated in the production process based on the principle of conservation of mass.

Article 26 Any enterprise, institution or other business operator that directly discharges taxable pollutants to the environment shall, in addition to paying environmental protection tax in accordance with the provisions of this Law, bear liability for the damage caused according to law.

Article 27 The State Council shall, based on the needs of national economic and social development and environmental protection, carry out pilot programs for the levy of environmental protection tax on enterprises, institutions and other business operators that directly discharge volatile organic compounds other than those specified in the Table of Taxable Pollutants and Equivalent Values appended to this Law. The pilot implementation measures shall be formulated by the State Council and submitted to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress for recordation.
The State Council and its relevant departments shall, based on the characteristics of volatile organic compounds, reasonably set the tax scope and tax rate range, improve monitoring technologies and emission calculation methods, strengthen work coordination, and accelerate the pilot work.
The State Council shall, within five years from the date of implementation of the pilot implementation measures, report to the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress on the pilot situation of levying environmental protection tax on volatile organic compounds and propose amendments to the law.

Article 28 As of the date on which this Law comes into force, environmental protection tax shall be levied in accordance with the provisions of this Law, and pollutant discharge fees shall no longer be levied.

Article 29 This Law shall come into force on January 1, 2018.
